jobs.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI
Principal Product Marketing Manager, AI Governance
Regulatory Counsel, AI Regulation, US
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY

reading.body:
AI governance hiring is senior-only and thin: five postings, every one at consultant level or above, concentrated in US tech hubs plus one in Munich.

The roles are not engineering roles. They are policy, legal, marketing, and finance functions, and the titles carry seniority markers rather than junior ones. Two of the five sit directly on the compute story. Cohere's public policy manager covers compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI. ServiceNow's FinOps lead governs AI spend, which is compute cost under another name.

That matters because governance work is where the physical constraints of AI get translated into rules and budgets. Sovereign AI and infrastructure policy are the terms under which siting, power, and cross-border compute get negotiated. A company hiring a policy manager for compute is treating the buildout as a regulatory and cost problem, not only a technical one.

Five postings are not a market. The data carries no salary, no time series, and no federal openings, even though USAJobs is among the sources drawn on. The postings span April to September 2026, but five dated points cannot show whether this hiring is rising or flat. The absence of other governance roles may reflect how the listings were collected rather than how many exist.
